newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight at 5.80 pct on lending by big banks.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight at 5.80 pct on lending by big banks.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 5.80 percent on Tuesday as big banks were long, and lent out funds in the overnight market, dealers said.
"The big banks as well as offshore banks remain long and they are still offering," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "Moreover, there are not many borrowers in the market."
Dealers said there has been speculation the central bank, through its agent banks, has been supporting the overnight from falling below its perceived floor of 5.80 percent.
The big banks, which were short earlier, now have excess funds due to recent borrowings and bills maturities.
Earlier, interbank rates also remained soft.
One-week money was at 7.20 percent against 7.40 percent on Monday.
One-month money was at 7.55 percent and three-month money at 7.60 percent. They were at 7.60/80 percent on Monday.

Dealers said rates have been pressured by improved liquidity following recent lending by the central bank and last week's maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 1.5 billion ringgit which were not rolled over.
There will be another maturity of a 500-million ringgit bill issue on Wednesday.

But dealers said an outgo of some two billion ringgit on Thursday due to maturity of funds Bank Negara lent to the market to help ease market tightness last month, could prevent rates from falling further.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange stayed firm on the back of softer cash interbank rates.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up one point to 92.56, or an implied yield of 7.44 percent.
The December contract also rose one to 92.67, or 7.33 percent and March 1998 was up two to 92.75, or 7.25 percent.
